extracted.intended_audience: corporate communications / PR professionals, crisis managers, and business continuity teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and lessons for corporate crisis public relations and social-media-driven incident response, illustrated by Domino’s 2009 YouTube prank case study. Intended to inform preparation, response, and post-crisis recovery actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release response in a timely manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Domino’s claimed that they had taken action by the time they were alerted to the video, they failed to show the public that they were on top of the situation. It took them 48 hours to release a statement that had led to additional outbursts from terrified customers and increased number of the prank video views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond quickly and visibly when alerted to an incident; multi-day delays (e.g., 48 hours) can amplify outrage and viewership. Being early reassures customers and reduces the 'perpetual mushroom effect of viral sensations.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Steer clear of using traditional communication strategy in social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Domino’s first response was to implement traditional strategy by trying to minimize the public attention on the issue. However ... the strategy failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating social media like traditional channels (i.e., trying to minimize attention). Instead, engage on the platforms where the incident originated and use social tactics suited to rapid, public, conversational environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver effective PR statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are a crucial part of crisis management, and many believe that Domino’s did a great job with their official statement to the video prank scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective crisis statements should: (1) show true sincerity that humanizes the brand, (2) clearly explain the measures being taken, (3) assure the public the situation will not happen again, and (4) include visible leadership (e.g., the president appearing). Use clear, sincere language and specific corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a loyal following on social media
rubrics_metrics.description: They were fortunate to be quickly notified by their staunch fans about the crisis. Otherwise, they might be too late to respond to the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate an engaged base of followers who will alert you to issues and amplify official messages. Assemble and prepare a social media team before crises occur so fans and staff can act as early detectors and messengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: A robust social media plan is a key part of crisis communication strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must ensure to integrate their marketing efforts with their online crisis response plans, especially before the crisis hits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an integrated digital marketing and crisis-response plan that defines roles, channels, messaging templates, escalation paths, and monitoring processes prior to any incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert the crisis into an opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Domino’s launched a campaign ad that leveraged the incident and utilized social media to collect feedback about their product; they also planned to implement their social media program and hired social media specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use crises as a chance to listen, collect customer feedback, iterate products/services, and publicly demonstrate improvement. Campaigns that honestly document fixes can restore trust and drive positive business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online surveillance / absence of online surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of online surveillance was listed as a failure point for Domino’s during the prank scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement continuous social listening and online surveillance to detect mentions, videos, and viral content early. Lack of monitoring delays response and increases reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of employee policy on social media use and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of employee policy on social media use and communication was identified as a problem in the Domino’s incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt clear employee social-media policies, training, and enforcement to reduce the risk of internal actors creating harmful content. Policies should define prohibited behaviors, reporting channels, and disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No social media presence
rubrics_metrics.description: No social media presence was cited as a cause of Domino’s slow detection/response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain active accounts on major platforms to enable direct customer engagement, rapid response, and official statements when incidents occur; absence leaves brand vulnerable and dependent on third-party narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond through the platform where the incident broke out / target core audience
rubrics_metrics.description: They decided to use the same channel where the incident broke out on. Posting an effective official statement on YouTube and creating an account on Twitter to engage with public became successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match your response channel to the origin and spread of the incident (e.g., respond on YouTube if a video went viral there). Target core audiences on the platforms they use to maximize reach and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create dedicated social accounts and engage directly
rubrics_metrics.description: The brand created a Twitter account to address the comments in the twitter space and engaged with bloggers and online commentators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack a presence on a platform where an incident is trending, create verified accounts or use existing official channels quickly to engage, answer questions, and correct misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit mistakes and be flexible to change communication strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to admit mistakes and flexible enough to change its communication strategy was listed among 'what went right.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly acknowledge wrongdoing or failures when factual, and be willing to pivot your communication approach (e.g., switch from minimizing to transparent apology) as the situation and audience reaction evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visible leadership to humanize the brand
rubrics_metrics.description: The response video had the president, Patrick Doyle, appear in the response video; later the CEO narrated the Pizza Turnaround documentary to show commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include senior leadership in messaging to convey accountability and seriousness; leader visibility helps humanize the company and demonstrate commitment to fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-driven product remediation and transparent documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: They came up with new recipes ... ran a research-driven marketing campaign called Pizza Turnaround ... hired a documentary film crew that shot focus group discussions and replayed the footage for management and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use research (focus groups, tracking studies) to diagnose product issues, document the improvement process publicly (e.g., videos), and invite customers to validate changes; transparency around remediation builds credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in technology and digital capabilities to build resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Domino’s invested in IT infrastructure: Domino’s Tracker, mobile ordering, AI bot Dom, in-car ordering, GPS delivery tracking, e-bikes and route-optimized locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop digital ordering, tracking, delivery optimizations and analytics to improve customer experience and make the business more resilient to external shocks (e.g., pandemics) and competitive pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases are a crucial part of crisis management
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are crucial part of crisis management, and many believe that Domino’s did a great job with their official statement to the video prank scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare clear, authoritative press releases as part of crisis playbooks; ensure they are sincere, factual, outline corrective measures, and are distributed through appropriate channels including platforms where the crisis is active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble and prepare a social media team before launch
rubrics_metrics.description: Tim McIntyre revealed that they had assembled their social media team a month before the incident. They were still working on a strategy for their social media launch when the prank video came out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form a trained social media/crisis team in advance with defined roles and escalation procedures so they can act immediately when an incident arises rather than building capacity reactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use negative incident as springboard for brand improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Used the negative incident as a springboard for better communications strategy and brand improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transform reputational setbacks into opportunities for product, operational, or communications improvements; publicly document changes to regain trust and demonstrate learning.
